delivered: F.shower gained three opt-in options -- divider ('n'|'s'|'e'|'w', a full-height frameless panel with a ceiling brace instead of that side's 2.0 m cabin pane; 'n' and 'w' had no pane at all before, so a divider there is a new panel), valve, handheld. Bathroom 2 sets divider 'w' (the side facing the bath), valve and handheld.

regressionGuard.callers: 7 F.shower callers across three apartments; exactly one changed.
regressionGuard.argument: With `divider` absent the refactor is provably identical: pane('s') resolves to PlaneGeometry(w, 2.0) at (0, 2.0/2 + 0.04, d/2) = (0, 1.04, d/2), and pane('e') to PlaneGeometry(d, 2.0) rotY PI/2 at (w/2, 1.04, 0) -- the same two meshes the old gl1/gl2 built.
regressionGuard.measured: Argument not trusted on its own. horkyone-10 -- an apartment this branch does not touch at all -- rendered at its shower (5.55, 4.6, yaw 180, 900x700, through the post chain) on BASE b78ebd3 (:8743) and HEAD (:8742), served simultaneously in one session.
regressionGuard.conclusion: BASE-vs-HEAD is SMALLER than the same-tree reload control on both pairings. Indistinguishable.
regressionGuard.sideFinding: horkyone-10's per-page-load spread at this camera is mean 2.01, against kings-court's 0.24 at its entry hall -- roughly eight times larger on the same machine in the same session. Plan 5 owns 'what varies across a page load'; this says the answer is not uniform across apartments, which a single-apartment probe would have missed.

gate.pairing: same session, BASE b78ebd3 on :8743 and HEAD on :8742
gate.reading: Metric-neutral, and that is expected rather than disappointing: the divider is transparent glass and the valve and handheld are small chrome parts. Every spot moved less than kings-court's ~0.35 per-spot noise floor.

notDelivered.derivation: Camera (9.3, 1.2) yaw 200 -> forward (0.342, 0.940); screen-right = cross(forward, up) = (-0.94, 0.342) = WEST; so screen-LEFT is EAST. The photograph puts the shower on the left, therefore EAST, and the bath WEST. The config has shower x 9.6-10.55 and bath x 10.55-11.35, i.e. the other way round. The old poseNote's claim is CONFIRMED by independent derivation.
notDelivered.whyNotFixed: Room interior is 2.46 x 2.46 m. The photographed side-by-side arrangement needs 1.7 (bath) + 0.95 (shower) = 2.65 m along one wall. Shortening the bath to 1.5 m makes 2.45 fit -- but the only orientation that then puts the shower east places the bath against the WEST wall, which carries this room's own door (opening at z 1.5-2.35), and CLAUDE.md rule 2a requires 0.5 m clear. Every remaining variant either buries the camera or blocks the door.
notDelivered.routed: plan 5, with serenity's sofa and mainCeilH. Same question in all three: whether the configured room is the right size, not where the fixture goes.

separateFinding.item: 14.webp's gate reading is scoring a wall
separateFinding.detail: Under the legacy gate camera (72 deg vertical, the population every gate number in this project is measured with) this spot renders a close-up of bare marble in BOTH trees -- no bath, no shower tray, no fixtures in frame. At the per-spot fov the same camera frames the room. So 14.webp's all-spot legacy dE2000 is not measuring the bathroom, which is worth knowing before anyone attributes a movement there to bathroom work.
separateFinding.routed: plan 5, folded into the existing meta.photoFovLong row (configured 120, measured ~57-58 by two independent methods).
